veranderings.voor: al baie fossiele van plante en van diere gekry
veranderings.na: al baie fossiele van plante en van diere gevind
veranderings.rede: 'gekry' for finding fossils is colloquial; 'gevind' is the standard written form and the lesson already uses it elsewhere.

veranderings.voor: fossiele van vroeë mense in die rotse gekry
veranderings.na: fossiele van vroeë mense in die rotse gevind
veranderings.rede: Same register fix as the previous sentence: 'gevind' rather than 'gekry'.

veranderings.voor: Dit beteken daar is hier baie fossiele en ook baie soorte.
veranderings.na: Dit beteken daar is baie fossiele hier, van baie soorte.
veranderings.rede: 'daar is hier baie fossiele' is stiff word order, and 'en ook baie soorte' leaves unclear what the kinds are of.

veranderings.blok: Hoekom lê hier so baie fossiele
veranderings.voor: Die Karoo is een van daardie dele en dit is
veranderings.na: Die Karoo is een van daardie dele, en dit is
veranderings.rede: AWS comma: 'en' joins two sentences that each have their own subject and verb.

veranderings.blok: Hoekom lê hier so baie fossiele
veranderings.voor: die regte soort rots vir fossiele om in te lê
veranderings.na: die regte soort rots vir fossiele
veranderings.rede: 'vir fossiele om in te lê' copies the English 'for fossils to lie in'; the shorter phrase says the same naturally.

veranderings.voor: is ook hier in ons land gekry
veranderings.na: is ook hier in ons land gevind
veranderings.rede: 'gevind' rather than colloquial 'gekry' for fossils found.

veranderings.na: Hierdie dinosourusse het in Afrika geleef
veranderings.rede: 'Hulle' could refer to the fossils just named, and animals 'leef' somewhere more naturally than they 'woon'.
'voetspore' is clearer for Grade 5 than bare 'spore', which can also mean traces or tracks in general.

veranderings.voor: 'n dier wat vandag lewe by mekaar pas
veranderings.na: 'n dier wat vandag lewe, by mekaar pas
veranderings.rede: A comma after the embedded relative clause shows where the subject ends, so the young reader does not read 'lewe by mekaar' together.

veranderings.voor: in 'n rots wat ons dolomiet noem
veranderings.na: in 'n soort rots wat ons dolomiet noem
veranderings.rede: 'in 'n rots' suggests one single rock; dolomite is a kind of rock, as the glossary says.

veranderings.voor: in daardie grotte al baie fossiele van vroeë mense gekry
veranderings.na: in daardie grotte al baie fossiele van vroeë mense gevind
veranderings.rede: 'gevind' rather than 'gekry', which also avoids 'gekry' twice in a row with 'sy naam gekry' in the next sentence.

veranderings.voor: Wêrelderfenisgebied en die grotte word beskerm
veranderings.na: Wêrelderfenisgebied, en die grotte word beskerm
veranderings.rede: AWS comma: 'en' joins two sentences that each have their own subject and verb.
The next sentence uses 'geleef'; one form throughout, and 'geleef' is the more common participle.
'hulle' directly follows 'vroeë mense', so it could be read as studying the people rather than the fossils.

veranderings.voor: 'n Groot vis diep in die see wat baie soos visse in fossiele lyk.
veranderings.na: 'n Groot vis wat diep in die see lewe en baie soos visse in fossiele lyk.
veranderings.rede: 'n Groot vis diep in die see wat...' hangs the place phrase on nothing; the study text's own verb 'lewe' makes it one clear relative clause.

vlae.teks: Al die fossiele wat in 'n plek se rotse bewaar gebly het.
vlae.rede: The study text defines a fossil record as all the fossils of 'n land', the glossary says 'n plek'; not changed because choosing one is a content decision.
